function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data as specified by the parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

**Paris** – the capital city of France – is one of the world’s most iconic urban centers, known for its rich history, art, fashion, cuisine, and cultural influence. | Topic | Highlights | |-------|------------| | **Location & Geography** | Situated in northern France along the Seine River, Paris covers roughly 105 km² (40 sq mi). The city is divided into 20 arrondissements (districts) that spiral clockwise from the center. | | **Population** | About 2.1 million residents live within the city limits (as of 2023), while the greater metropolitan area (Île‑de‑France) houses ~12 million people. | | **History** | • Founded in the 3rd century BCE as a Gallic settlement (Lutetia).
• Became the capital of the Frankish kingdom in the 8th century.
• Major events: Renaissance, Revolution (1789), World Wars, and the modern era of global diplomacy. | | **Landmarks & Attractions** | • **Eiffel Tower** – 330 m iron lattice, built 1889.
• **Notre‑Dame de Paris** – Gothic cathedral (rebuilt after 2019 fire).
• **Louvre Museum** – home to the Mona Lisa, 35,000+ works.
• **Arc de Triomphe**, **Palace of Versailles** (just outside the city), **Sainte‑Chapelle**, **Montmartre** hill, **Luxembourg Gardens**. | | **Culture & Arts** | • Birthplace of Impressionism (Monet, Renoir).
• Hosts major fashion weeks (Fall/Winter, Spring/Summer).
• Vibrant theater scene: Opéra Garnier, Comédie‑Française. | | **Cuisine** | • Famous for croissants, baguettes, cheese (Camembert, Brie), wine, and haute cuisine.
• Culinary institutions: Le Cordon Bleu, Michelin‑starred restaurants. | | **Transportation** | • Extensive metro network (14 lines, ~300 stations).
• RER commuter trains, buses, trams, bike‑share (Velib’).
• Two major airports: Charles de Gaulle (CDG) and Orly (ORY). | | **Economy** | • Major financial hub: headquarters of BNP Paribas, Société Générale, and many multinational corporations.
• Strong tourism sector; ~30 million visitors annually pre‑COVID. | | **Education & Research** | • Prestigious universities: Sorbonne, Sciences Po, École Normale Supérieure.
• Leading research institutes in physics, medicine, humanities. | | **Climate** | Oceanic climate: mild winters (~5 °C), warm summers (~25 °C). Rainfall fairly evenly distributed year‑round. | --- ### Quick Facts | Fact | Value | |------|-------| | **Official language** | French | | **Time zone** | Central European Time (CET) / Central European Summer Time (CEST) | | **Currency** | Euro (€) | | **Area** | 105 km² | | **Mayor (2023)** | Anne Hidalgo (PS) | | **Notable festivals** | Bastille Day (14 July), Fête de la Musique (21 June), Nuit Blanche (first Friday of October) | --- #### Want to know more? - **Travel tips**: Best times to visit, must‑see neighborhoods, public transport hacks. - **Historical deep dive**: Key events that shaped modern Paris. - **Culinary guide**: Where to eat, food markets, cooking classes. - **Art & museum itinerary**: Suggested routes for first‑time visitors.
